subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should agent-visible WebChat client type be exposed as gateway-attested connect metadata, as an explicitly untrusted diagnostic hint, or not exposed to agents yet?
rationale: Agents may use client type for native-only behavior, deep links, diagnostics, or privileged UX, so automation cannot safely choose the trust semantics or carrier shape.

options.title: Expose Gateway-Attested Metadata
options.body: Propagate validated `connect.client` identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document what agents may trust.

options.title: Expose Untrusted Diagnostic Hint
options.body: Surface only a clearly labeled untrusted hint for debugging and forbid agents from treating it as a capability or permission signal.

options.title: Defer Runtime Exposure
options.body: Keep client identity limited to Gateway diagnostics until a stronger client-attestation design exists.

recommendation.title: Expose Gateway-Attested Metadata
recommendation.body: Propagate validated `connect.client` identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document what agents may trust.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Gateway protocol, WebSocket, chat runtime, and trust-boundary ownership where steipete has the strongest recent history.
